The most notable features of the system are to be found in the proposed approach to Rayleigh fading simulation, realized on a PC in an easy and flexible form, which can be conveniently interfaced to external hardware devices for measurement and test purposes. In modeling the Rayleigh channel, the classic Gilbert's model was modified, maintaining on the one hand its simple structure but avoiding on the other hand some inherent drawbacks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the design of communication systems by ECCS and CSP based approaches
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors deal with two important behavioral techniques: communicating sequential processes (CSP) and the calculus for communicating systems (CCS). The authors introduce the syntax and meaning of CSP constructs and discuss CSP specifications and proofs. By way of illustration, the authors present the CSP specification of a transport protocol and its verification. The syntax and semantics of ECCS (extended CCS) and a technique for performing proofs about ECCS specifications are given. The ECCS specification and verification of a bus controller are also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An object-oriented approach to directory systems
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The author sums up the experience of designing and implementing a prototype directory system based on the standards jointly produced by CCITT and the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). The open systems approach is adopted in designing the system. The prototype includes an object-oriented database implemented on top of a commercial relational database for storing directory information and knowledge. With this design, a new communication stack would only mean a slightly different front-end process. The behavioral encapsulation provided by the object-oriented database guarantees that any object-oriented database can be used to replace the current back-end database system with a minimum of effort.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The impact of changing markets and technologies on network strategies towards the 21st century
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Telecommunications markets in the 1990s are categorized broadly into consolidation, growth, and expansion opportunities. The author briefly examines the role of changing markets and technological advances in network strategies as they progress toward the next century. Optical fiber has revolutionized telecommunications networks, with the main impact in the interexchange network. The next generation switching elements are being influenced by the effects of optical fiber related technology. The signaling and intelligence associated with networks are considered to be control elements, facilitating and enhancing the call process and capabilities. These parallel developments in transmission switching and control elements are being combined in the broadband integrated-services digital network (B-ISDN), concept.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel method for representing industrial inspection pattern
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A critical step in industrial pattern inspection is to design an effective and flexible method for representing the inspected pattern. The authors propose a novel representation method called pattern attributed hypergraph (PAHG). The PAHG is used to describe the pictorial information of the input pattern, which includes attributed nodes, connectivity between nodes (intrarelation), regional primitives, and neighborhood relations between regions (spatial interrelation). It is found that the complexity of graph matching with the PAHG structure is much lower than the corresponding complexity of the graph structure used by A.M. Darwish and A.K. Jain (1988). The reduced complexity is approximately 1/K/sup 2/ of the original, where K is the number of regions in the inspected pattern. It provides a better and faster approach for industrial pattern inspection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An overview of Hong Kong's international telecommunications operations
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: An overview of the wide range of telecommunication services provided in Hong Kong is given. The network of communication and computer switching systems that support the services is described. The considerations in international communications operations that are essential in providing secure and high-quality services are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high reliability VSAT transmitter using direct RF modulation
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors present the improvement in reliability in a very small aperture terminal (VSAT) using direct modulation as compared to the conventional VSAT. The reliability of the conventional and the direct modulation VSAT are exhaustively analyzed in quantitative terms. For the purpose of reliability analysis, the equipment is divided into standard functional blocks. Failure rates are established for these standard blocks, which are then used to calculate the overall reliability. The overall reliability of the VSAT is improved by nearly 36% by using a direct modulation transmitter as compared to the conventional VSAT. However, when the transmit path of the VSAT alone is compared, the improvement is nearly 75%. The analysis was done for a single channel per carrier (SCPC)-type VSAT using frequency division multiple access (FDMA). A similar analysis was also done for a VSAT employing a code division multiple access (CDMA) scheme. The results are summarized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Estimating two-dimensional directions of arrival of narrow band sources
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A new approach to making high-resolution estimates of two-dimensional (2-D) directions of arrival (DOA) of multiple narrowband sources for a rectangular sensor array is presented. By fully using the properties of the autocovariance and cross-covariance matrices, the authors construct a new matrix called the generalized DOA matrix method. Theoretical analysis shows that 2-D signal direction vectors may be obtained from the eigendecomposition of the generalized DOA matrix. Without 2-D searches, the method is highly efficient in computation. Simulation results are given to illustrate its good performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance modeling of two phase service policy in distributed systems
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A Markovian queuing system is used to model a two-phase service (TPS) system. In this system, there are two queues, batch queue and individual queue, and a central server switching service between them. Expressions of mean task response time in the TPS are derived from the Markov chain concept and the Z-transform technique. Other performance parameters, such as the concept of power and speedup, and the optimization issues are also taken into consideration. Furthermore, the performance improvement issue is investigated and the speedup upper bound is therefore obtained. Finally, numerical results are provided to verify the analytical model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An alternative formula for performance evaluation of unbuffered multistage interconnection networks
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors present a formula to evaluate the performance of unbuffered multistage interconnection networks (MINs), with emphasis on MINs composed of 2*2 switching elements. In this formula, the normalized throughput of an unbuffered MIN is expressed in terms of the input rate and the number of states. The new formula is proved by mathematical induction. The major advantage of this formula is that the asymptotic behavior of an unbuffered MIN can be easily determined. It is shown that the formula results in the same asymptotic performance as that obtained by C.P. Kruskal and M. Snir (1983). In addition to analyzing the asymptotic behavior, the formula can be applied to evaluate the exact performance of unbuffered MINs. The formula is generalized for unbuffered MINs in the presence of nonidentical input rates.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dynamic programming and cue-generation for automatic vehicle model identification
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors describe an application of dynamic programming based matching to vehicle identification. An edge map is first generated and various preprocessing stages are carried out culminating in the use of a two-dimensional Hough transform to generate a cued region containing a putative car. A dynamic programming search (edge list search) is then carried out to identify the type of car, e.g. Citroen, Lada, mini, van etc., within the located area. This model identification method has been applied to a number of different real images and has been found to be successful. Illustrative results are given. Even when the shape is fragmented and embedded in the background, the matching between the reference shape and image will automatically identify the set of observed segments that best match the reference shape.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new two-view stereo matching method and its application
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors describe a new two-view stereo image matching method which is quite effective for a kind of object called block objects. The matching technique uses local geometric constraints among edges, corners and the two-view stereo images to resolve matching ambiguity. The authors describe its application in object recognition and localization. Some experimental results are given to illustrate the effect of applying it to the two-view stereo vision system. Compared with other matching methods, the proposed matching technique is simple, effective, rapid and has a high corrective match rate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Error performance of digital microwave transmission system
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors present the principal characteristics of the error-detection system and error analysis based on error field measurement in a digital microwave transmission system. The error performance and propagation field trial was carried out by using a standby channel of 34 Mb/s and another digital path of 64 kb/s. The authors obtained information about errors and reached some conclusions by analyzing the data obtained. The error distribution of the 34 Mb/s hierarchy is summarized by long-term bit error field trials. The relationships between the degraded minutes (DM) objective, the severely errored seconds (SES) objective at 64 kb/s, and the corresponding parameters at the system bit rate according to the error's stochastic allotment are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New technologies for optical submarine systems
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Two different technologies are presently under consideration for a new generation of optical submarine systems: the regeneration, direct extrapolation of the present technology, which could be used for system installation as early as the end of 1994, and direct optical amplification, a totally new technology, which may appear as the technology of the future. The generations of optical submarine systems follow one another very quickly: 280 Mb/s across the Atlantic in 1988, 560 Mb/s in 1991, and probably 2.5 Gb/s by 1995. The author describes the technology of the 560 Mb/s system using regeneration, which is presently under development. The technologies of regeneration and direct optical amplification which could be developed for the future 2.5 Gb/s system are considered, and the difficulties of both development programs are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analytical studies of superposition GMDP traffic sources for ATM networks
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The generally modulated deterministic process (GMDP) model has been introduced within the European commission RACE program. The superposition of GMDP traffic sources can be so complicated that the superposition of n k-state traffic sources can have up to (n+k-1)-factorial divided by n-factorial times (k-1)-factorial states. The authors present an efficient approach to reduce the number of states for superposed traffic sources to n*(k-1)+1 by selecting associated cell rates of the states and combining the superposed states with the same cell rates together. Therefore, the traffic sources can be characterized more precisely by using more states without increasing the complexity of the superposed traffic sources. The authors show that the superposed traffic sources become smoother when the number of traffic sources increases.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Event abstraction for debugging distributed programs
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The author presents the first analytical study of event abstraction for debugging distributed programs. The results of the study give a better understanding of the impact of event abstraction on event precedences. It shows that a higher-level behavior model provides a correct picture of the precedence relation if and only if all events in the behavior model are contractions. Also, it is shown that most event abstraction systems indeed preserve event precedence since they only support simple contraction. This study not only provides guidelines for developing an abstraction-based distributed debugging system, but also has wider implications in system specification language, programming languages and operating systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fabrication and characterisation of rare earth doped optical fibres
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors compare the properties of fibers with P co-doped cores to those with Ge and Al co-doped cores. Rare-earth doped fibers with various compositions have been fabricated and characterized. P co-doped fibers have significant advantages as amplifiers compared with other co-dopants. The excited state absorption is greatly reduced at the 1300-nm window in a P co-doped Nd/sup 3+/ fiber. Furthermore, the excited state absorption in Er/sup 3+/ doped fibers for 514.5-nm pumping is also significantly reduced. As a result, the largest gain yet reported (1.6 dB/mW) in such fiber using this pump wavelength was measured. The absorption, fluorescence and gain spectrum indicates that P co-doping offers improvements over conventional co-dopants such as Ge and Al.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Negative electrical feedback grinrod external coupled cavity semiconductor laser
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Presents a new configuration of a negative frequency feedback semiconductor laser. Instead of a Fabry-Perot etalon, an optical fiber ring resonator is used as the FM noise detector. All the components are connected by optical fibers. The spectral linewidth of the 1.3- mu m graded-index-rod external coupled cavity (GRECC) InGaAsP BH laser diode is narrowed by using the negative electrical feedback technique. The linewidth-power product and the minimum spectral linewidth are 3.4 MHz-mW and 850 kHz, respectively.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A threefold multiple access protocol for integrated data/voice local area networks
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A threefold multiple-access protocol (TMAP) is proposed for bus-structured integrated voice/data local area networks, which is the combination of CSMA/CD, reservation and implicit token protocols. When the network is lightly loaded, the voice stations, and data stations operate at the CSMA/CD mode, when the load increases, the voice stations have to reserve transmission of all voice packets. Under heavy loads, the implicit token is merely delivered to voice stations, and the data stations have to defer until the network returns to reservation mode. TMAP is distributed and can support networks with large size and high speed. A simulation study and is comparison with a hybrid protocol are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Educational computer systems using erasable programmable logic devices
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: An overview is provided of erasable programmable logic device (EPLD)-based experiments on computer subsystems and systems. The author discusses the educational issues on digital/computer systems design. Computers with either parallel or serial internal architectures have been implemented using EPLDs and a static-RAM chip. The EPLD-based experiments have provided students with a good introduction to one form of ASIC (application specific integrated circuit) technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the Petrinet modelling of medium access protocols
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors deal with the modelling and performance analysis of a medium-access protocol used in token-ring networks. The model is based on the advanced Petri net (APN) proposed by the authors (1987) and by K.S. Sivananden (1988). A brief overview of the APN is given. It is shown that the APN is a versatile modelling and analysis tool, as it incorporates such features as coloured tokens, source and sink places and transitions with flexible firing rules and finite firing times. A local-area network (LAN) of four stations, with token-ring topology is considered. It is shown that all aspects of the medium-access protocol can be readily and effectively modelled by the APN. Analysis of the net is undertaken for performance evaluation. Such an evaluation has been made possible due to the availability of appropriate analysis techniques with the APN.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The Melbourne University heterogeneous multiprocessor
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The Melbourne University heterogeneous multiprocessor is an experimental multiple-input multiple-data (MIMD) multiprocessor with different processing elements and is based on a shared memory architecture. The authors discuss the overall structure of the multiprocessor, and concentrate on the bus arbitration and the synchronization techniques used. Results based on a parallel implementation of the Sieve of Eratosthenes are presented. The results indicate that for a three-processor system, the memory contention is fairly small (even though the processors access the common memory repeatedly), and that the heterogeneous multiprocessor achieves a good speedup over the uniprocessor system (approximately 1.5*) for a small increase in cost.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optical waveguides by silver-sodium ion exchange process in nitrate mixtures
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Planar-graded index optical waveguides have been fabricated in soda lime glass substrates by silver (Ag/sup +/) ion exchange in a mixed melt of silver nitrate (AgNO/sub 3/), potassium nitrate (KNO/sub 3/) and sodium nitrate (NaNO/sub 3/). The propagation mode indices measured agree well with the theoretical WKB dispersion relation of J.W. White and P.F. Heidrich (1976) using a second-order polynomial function for the refractive index profile. The surface index change can be varied from 0.09 to 0.004 by changing the amount of AgNO/sub 3/ in the mixed nitrate melt, and effective diffusion coefficients have been calculated for these waveguides.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the structure and the adjustment of the all-fiber isolator
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The working principle of the all-fiber isolator and the decrease of isolation degree caused by some imperfections in real devices are discussed. If the polarization rotating angle of a Faraday rotator is 45 degrees exactly, the maximum isolation degree of the isolator equals the extinction ratio of the polarizer. The authors simplify the analysis by assuming the extinction ratio of the polarizer is infinite, attempting to approach this limit of maximum isolation degree as closely as possible. Analysis and experiment prove that by using two polarization controllers the highest isolation ratio and the smallest insertion loss can be obtained simultaneously. The adjusting principle of the device is also explained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A codebook design algorithm for vector quantization of images
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors present a new codebook design algorithm for the vector quantization of images. A two-dimensional discrete cosine transform (DCT) is used to extract the feature vectors of training images. Using the good energy compact capability of DCT, certain significant components of the feature vectors are extracted and then used to partition the training vectors into a binary tree. This results in a significant savings of computation in the clustering process. Simulation results show that the new algorithm requires about 51% of the amount of time needed by the pairwise nearest neighbor (PNN) algorithm and a better reconstructed picture quality is obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multi-processor multi-channel PCM test system
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The design and development of a pulse code modulated (PCM) test system are described. For real-time signaling analysis, a TMS320C25 digital signal processor (DSP)-based card is designed to interface with the IBM PC input/output (I/O) channel. This card is designed for multichannel signal analysis and an associated software is written for multifrequency compelled (MFC) digital analysis. A chip set from Mitel is also used to interface to the 30-channel PCM (2048 kb/s) system. This card is designed to cater for clock extraction and regeneration from the PCM data, synchronization checks, time-slot selection and the extraction of signaling data which is then passed to the PC via dual-port RAMs. An onboard 80188 microprocessor is also incorporated in the design to act as a front-end processor and to initialize and control the PCM interface. Test results show that the prototype functions as expected.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ATM switching system architecture and implementation of B-ISDN
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The author describes an asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) switching system that used high-speed ICs to provide multimedia traffic control and media-specific service adaptation. The architecture for ATM switching, which is called multi-stage self-routing (MSSR), is based on the self-routing switching principle of K. Hajikano et al. (1988). It is constructed by connecting self-routing switching modules in a three-stage link configuration. This system is a first implementation of the broadband-integrated services digital network (B-ISDN).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of pools of processors with hierarchical bus structure
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors consider a multiprocessor network, having pools of processing elements (PEs) interconnected with a hierarchical bus structure, suitable for real-time process control applications. The modeling, analysis and performance evaluation of such a network having three hierarchical levels is presented. The access patterns at different hierarchical levels are prioritized and access times are generalized to enable study of different connection time patterns. A semi-Markov process is developed to characterize the behavior of the network. The input parameters to the model are detailed. The different levels of interprocessor communication are parameterized and the various performance measures obtained are given. The analytical results are validated with simulation and the deviation observed was within 9% of simulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Finite element modelling of cardiac mechanics
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Echocardiographic short axis and two-chamber images were used to generate two- and three-dimensional models of the ventricles using finite brick elements. The cardiac borders were extracted by an automated edge detection algorithm. Subsequently, heuristic feature extraction determined the true shape of the heart throughout the cardiac cycle. Mechanical properties were assigned on the basis of reported myocardial tissue characteristics. The finite-element method was used to estimate elastic deformation at each brick in the ventricles. Dynamic displays of deformation were generated to provide a visual animation of cardiac mechanics throughout the cardiac cycle. The results allow quantitative analysis of regional wall dynamics and wall stress.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Real time image transfer on high speed local area network (integrated digital ring network)
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors present a scheme where real-time video data can be transmitted in an integrated service local-area network which provides multiple services, multiple channels, and multiple trains. A buffer insertion scheme with a random access protocol and a dynamic priority control scheme guarantee that the real-time data are transmitted within a certain amount of delay. Multiple transmissions can take place simultaneously. A priority control scheme ensures that the most urgent real-time video data are served first among the multiple services.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance characterization for a dual-channel multimedia multiplexer
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: An efficient system for simultaneously multiplexing a large number of isochronous and asynchronous data channels over a much smaller number of communication channels is presented. The multiplexer uses a dual-channel as a switching media. Perfect time-division multiplexing scheduling for the carrier-sense channel is achieved. Each DSO channel of a T1 trunk is addressable. The high switching efficiency comes from the employment of the digital signal energy detection in each isochronous DSO channel. Voice and real-time data are multiplexed synchronously. The exact formula of the delay-throughput analysis for the asynchronous data is derived. The effect of mean voice talkspurts length is addressed for the delay performance of the asynchronous data traffic. When no hangover time is added to the speech energy detection, the asynchronous data packet delay time is proven to be very small.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The competition model-a comparison
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The competition model is a parallel execution model for logic programs developed in the same framework as the AND/OR process model supporting both AND- and OR-parallelism. It allows a high degree of parallelism, avoids the reconstruction of the data dependency graph, and causes fewer literals to be reset. The competition model is presented and then compared with other AND/OR process models. The competition model consists of two algorithms: the forward execution algorithm and the backward execution algorithm. In the presentation of each algorithm, an informal description is given before the formal algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Data driven C-a concurrent programming language
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Data driven C (DDC) is a new concurrent programming language designed for machines with message passing architecture. The concurrent programming extensions to C are based on the simple rendezvous concept. The authors discuss the creation of a process, interaction between processes and the integrated module in DDC. A process is the most basic computation unit in a DDC program. A process with large grain size tends to incur less communication cost. Hence, DDC encourages programmers to create a large grain process by requiring each process to be declared separately with a process header. DDC integrates component processes into a reusable integrated module. The main contribution of DDC is its introduction of a socket as a flexible channel naming scheme and a concurrent code packaging technique called the integrated module.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fast finding the steady solution of an elastic system (dynamic train weighing system)
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A real elastic system, a dynamic train weighing system, is presented. It is necessary to find the steady solution of the system in a few seconds while a pulse force is applied to the system. There are considerable elastic vibrations and some noise. The nearest-mean filter with some compensation is used to find the steady-state solution of the system. More than forty dynamic weighing experiments show that the processing of the nearest-mean filter is effective. All of the errors are less than +or-0.2%. It reaches the national and international standards of a train weighing system. The signal processing of the nearest-mean filter and the decimation narrowband filter are introduced to process the weighing signal during motion. They are very effective in improving the processing precision of weighing data in motion at different velocities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A sweeping line algorithm based on two dimensional region search
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors present a new plane-sweep algorithm which is based on several primitive functions of region query for a number of overlapped rectangles in 2-D space. A theorem proves that the presented algorithm can be built from any spatial data structure with region query functions. Experimental results presented show that this algorithm has been successfully implemented in C language based on two kinds of spatial data structures, the multiple storage quad tree and the quad list quad tree. This algorithm can be performed in a time complexity of O(N log N).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On an efficient decomposition of LPC excitation for producing natural sounding speech
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors present a new method of modeling the excitation of the linear predictive coding (LPC) synthesis filter at low and medium bit rates. For the speech segments with regular patterns, the excitation is composed of two sequences of pulses. The first sequence is generated in a way similar to the classical physical model that consists of a glottal filter with thinned coefficients driven by a set of pitch pulses. Both the glottal function and pitch pulses are determined using the analysis-by-synthesis technique with the mean square criterion. The auxiliary sequence consists of a few pulses to supplement the first sequence for further reducing the mean square error. For unvoiced speech segments, multipulse excitation is simply used to drive the synthesis filter. Based on real speech analysis, the model has a gain on signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 2-3 dB for voiced segments over the multipulse LPC using 0.8-2.5 pulses/ms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interoperable communications in the ISDN environment
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The author discusses the interoperable communications issues for heterogeneous systems connected to an ISDN. The author describes the role of open systems interconnection (OSI) in telecommunications networks and services, then briefly presents ISDN protocol modeling and it applications. Finally, some technical issues concerning the future network concept are addressed, with some consideration given to the architecture of intelligent communications network and evolution into broadband ISDN.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a programmable blind equalizer for high speed multilevel data transmission
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors describe the design and implementation of a two-dimensional adaptive blind equalizer for high-speed multilevel data transmission. The whole hardware of the blind equalizer consists of two printed circuit boards, one of which is used for the main part of the equalizer and the other for the automatic gain controllers and the analog-to-digital and the digital-to-analog converters. The area per board is about 400 cm/sup 2/. Owing to the use of the error control function and the TMS320C25 and DSP56200 digital processors, the equalizer possesses some good properties such as flexibility, versatility, small size, low cost, etc. The test results demonstrate excellent equalizer performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ISDN deployment-planning and building a corporate network
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors discuss the process a customer, AT&T Bell Laboratories, went through to determine their integrated services digital network (ISDN) requirements and implementation strategy. This information was derived from work required to plan the installation and service of over 10000, ISDN Centrex lines provided to AT&T Bell Laboratories. Planning for this network, one of the largest to fully utilize ISDN, involved a team of Bell Laboratories engineers with representatives from several areas (e.g., systems engineering, software development, and telecommunications). This team, by utilizing traditional tools and developing new and innovative techniques, determined end-user requirements for both voice and data. ISDN services in the United States in general are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Concept to reality-perspective on ISDN implementation
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Summary form only given. The author made a presentation on the integrated services digital network (ISDN) demonstration in February 1990 between AT&T of the US, and KDD and NTT of Japan. The demonstration utilized terminals from Japanese and US vendors, all operating on basic rate interfaces (BRIs) multiplexed via AT&T's 4ESS-based primary rate ISDN interface, and switched digital international service at 64 kb/s from New York City utilizing the AT&T-KDD international network to NTT ISN basic rate ISDN interfaces at demonstration sites in Tokyo and Osaka, Japan. Based on the experiences of AT&T, KDD, and NTT, the author provided an overview of the trial including the architecture and terminals involved. Compatibility and interoperability issues at the interface and application levels were also addressed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis by synthesis adaptive predictive correlated speech coding
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A correlated encoding strategy called the finite-state vector quantizer for correlated encoding (FSVQ-CEC) for the analysis-by-synthesis adaptive predictive speech coding (ASAPC) speech system is developed, which exploits the redundancy between vocal tract information and excitation information. Coding efficiencies have been obtained by taking advantage of the correlation among the speech samples or frames. The correlated characteristics between vocal tract parameters and excitational ones of these coders are first described and the correlated encoding strategies are presented. To demonstrate the simulation results and effectiveness of FSVQ-CEC, the authors apply FSVQ-CEC to linear-Gaussian observation and compare its rate-distortion performance with a theoretical bound.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The implementation of a PC-based list processor for symbolic computation
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors present the design and the evaluation results of the arithmetical symbolical list processor (ASLP), a purpose-built processor for list handling and processing. Multiple buses and multiple memory principles are applied for pipelining and parallel data movements. This microprogrammable ASLP is a stand-alone processor which connects to an IBM/AT personal computer. The IBM/AT personal computer works as the host of software development. The prototype of the ASLP is constructed using standard chips. A special micro-assembler is written for the ASLP micro-assembly program translation. Most standard list functions are programmed and evaluated. In parallel with the evaluation, the core part of the original hardware design of the ASLP is being redesigned using ASICs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ISDN BRI D-channel data characteristics and performance
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors present the results obtained from integrated services digital network (ISDN) basic rate interface (BRI) D-channel data users. Emphasis is given to the general data characteristics and the data services performance. The authors describe the D-channel data applications, the data collection setups, the ISDN data user characteristics, and the user data performance. The D-channel data service is flexible for various applications at or below 9.6 kb/s. The study shows that the data performance is acceptable for most data users' applications. All the results presented here were obtained from a single switch environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new microcomputer based imaging system with C/sup 3/ technique
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: To address the needs of a variety of image processing applications, a new microcomputer-based imaging system using color cell compression (C/sup 3/) and C/sup 3/-virtual techniques is presented. It is a primary object of the new imaging system to provide an improved digital color imaging system which produces excellent quality images and a high degree of versatility while using an extremely small amount of encoded data. These new imaging systems apply a digital signal processor (DSP) to speed up the compression scheme, which can help the system to operate in real time.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fast arithmetic computing with neural networks
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors introduce a restricted model of a neuron which is more practical as a model of computation then the classical model of a neuron. The authors define a model of neural networks as a feedforward network of such neurons. Whereas any logic circuit of polynomial size (in n) that computes the product of two n-bit numbers requires unbounded delay, such computations can be done in a neural network with constant delay. The authors improve some known results by showing that the product of two n-bit numbers and sorting of n n-bit numbers can both be computed by a polynomial size neural network using only four unit delays, independent of n. Moreover, the weights of each threshold element in the neural networks require only O(log n)-bit (instead of n-bit) accuracy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optical fiber video interactive system for IBIS
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The interactive business information systems (IBIS) project is described, and future trends in system design and the components required for such systems are discussed. The author examines the capabilities of such new components and their feasibilities in terms of the present state of the art and future potential capability as well as some new high technology such as superconductivity and biodevices. The author also briefly describes the highly interactive optical visual information system (Hi-OVIS) experiment, which is the first major interactive fiber-optic video information system. IBIS (Advanced Hi-OVIS) is a digital interactive optical visual information system which has been designed and developed with the same intent as that of Hi-OVIS.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Is continued fraction a representational basis for neuronal computing?
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The author examines the question of whether the continued fraction (CF) is a representational basis for neuronal computing. It is argued that when real or complex numbers are represented by physical quantities such as voltage, current, impedance, etc. and handled using bio-hardware, a natural mathematical representation that supports algorithmic manipulation is the CF. Arguments are provided from network theory, neural network models and distributed algorithm design. In particular, a matrix inversion free linear time algorithm based on CF is described for temporal rational interpolation that can be used for the design of impulse response filters, in conjunction with Laplace or z-transforms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Quantization error in ternary delta modulation schemes (image bandwidth compression)
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Image bandwidth compression using differential encoding is reviewed. The ternary delta modulation scheme, being simple to implement and efficient in bit-rate reduction, has been used. A method of pixel differences has been used to overcome the sensitivity problems and two prediction algorithms are shown. The quantizer used is based on the constant area quantization (CAQ) proposed by J.J. Pearson (1975), originally used for imaging by remote pilotless vehicles. The CAQ scheme used one-bit prediction and is included for comparison purposes. The relative positions of the basis pixels are shown. The quantization error of the scheme which arises from the use of the ternary quantizer imposes fundamental limitations on the quality of the reconstruction of images. Theoretical modeling as well as actual measurements of the mean square error are included.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: FDDI-II capacity analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The author analyzes the capacity of fiber distributed data interface (FDDI)-II for handling voice only traffic, multimedia traffic (voice+images of three different quality levels) and video traffic. The author compares the capacity of voice only FDDI-II applications with typical industry products. The analysis of the capacity for multimedia applications is extended to study a tandem ring configuration for supporting wide area traffic distribution. The video capacity analysis includes still and full motion. It is shown that a single-ring FDDI-II can handle 9000 phones or over 2000 multimedia stations or 240 video stations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A model for neurocomputing
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors propose a new model for neural computation based solely on a pattern recognition mechanism. By using pattern recognition as the basis of neurocomputing, the authors demonstrate that such a model can solve nonnumeric problems quickly, but it becomes very slow in solving numeric problems. Decisions in problem solving are also made through pattern matching. The outcome of matching is weighted to reflect appropriately the neurological basis. The complexity of computation is defined in terms of pattern matching operations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Applications of fiber optic communications in Hong Kong
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Fiber-optic communications in Hong Kong are reviewed. The aspects examined are the junction networks; optical systems; the local network; wideband services; and future trends in wavelength division multiplexing (WDM), synchronous optical network (SONET), metropolitan area networks (MAN), fiber to the home, and asynchronous transfer mode (ATM). In 1981, fiber-optic transmission was introduced. Now, over 95% of all interexchange connections are digital, and 75% use optical fiber. The digital transmission hierarchy used observes North American standards.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Real-time software design-from theory to practice
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: To understand the challenge ahead in real-time software design, the author examines the role timing considerations play in system design, the limitations of current design methods, and the major issues that must be resolved to bring theory to practice in the design of future real-time systems. Some of the major issues in mechanizing the specification, validation/verification and synthesis of the control structure of real-time software are highlighted. The author outlines some of the major research issues that must be considered in order to provide a rigorous foundation for automating the design chores that deal with timing constraints.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A graph theoretic approach for knowledge organisation on rulebased systems
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors discuss a graph theoretic approach to organize knowledge in rule-based systems to make them complete, concise and consistent. The topics discussed are: knowledge organization in expert systems development; knowledge representation using data structures; production rules; semantic nets; frames; and the necessity for knowledge organization. A graph theoretic approach for knowledge organization is presented, and an algorithm for knowledge organization is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PDP network density estimation
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Based on the assumption that most probability densities in real life can be approximated by a mixture of Gaussian densities, the authors propose a set of algorithms for training a multilayered perceptron as a parallel distributed processing network (PDP) to estimate various probability densities and serve as a Bayes classifier. The effectiveness of a PDP density estimator was measured in terms of the relative difference between the target probability density function and the network output representing the estimation. The classification rate of the PDP network was effectively identical to that of the Bayes classifier.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated optic devices for microwave applications
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Integrated optic devices designed for use in microwave applications are reviewed and the prospects for these new technologies are discussed. First, the modulation of light at microwave frequencies is briefly summarized. Then integrated optical circuits containing high-performance modulators are presented. Efficient light modulation at millimeter-wave frequencies is discussed. Finally, possible applications of high-speed light modulators are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of trellis-coded modulation on imperfect coherent detection
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: For the same signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of a phase reference, the sensitivity to the phase offset for an 8-phase-shift keying (8-PSK) scheme is greater than for uncoded quaternary phase-shift keying (QPSK). The effect of imperfect coherent detection is evaluated. The authors introduce the concept of equivalent distance on the basis of the conventional distance metric. By using the equivalent distances, the corresponding upper bound can be approached. Simulation results for the event error probability are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An expert system for failure analysis and disposition of hard disk drives
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors describe the development of an expert system for failure analysis and disposition of hard disk drives. A working prototype was implemented in the form of a run-time version and tried out on the production floor. The system is capable of providing consultation for forty-nine symptoms of failure from the four test stations. This includes twenty-nine debug procedures with due consideration to past records. Six evaluation test results are presented here to elaborate the efficiency and reliability of the system. These test runs were simulated on three test stations (recalibration, analog and burn-in). Besides providing logical and accurate consultation, the developed expert system can also be used as a teaching aid for new staff and serves to document the test procedures involved in hard disk testing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison of standard G3 and ECM G3 transmission using computer simulation
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Performance models for standard Group 3 (G3) and error correction mode (ECM) G3 fax transmission are investigated, and channels over the public switched telephone network (PSTN) are simulated. Transmission times under certain line conditions for the models are then compared and analyzed. The channel noise over PSTN was investigated. The transmission times at different error rates for the respective models are plotted. Samples of this curve have been verified with experiments. The bit error rate for an acceptable image quality on a predefined distortion vector is derived and used as the fallback rate for 9600 bps in STD mode.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new recognition method for partial 2-D perspective shapes
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors present a new method for the recognition of partial two-dimensional (2-D) perspective shapes. The method can identify the unknown shape directly from one image taken by a camera from an arbitrary perspective. The approach derives the geometrical relationship between the image frame and the object frame, develops the mapping formula to recover the shape from the perspective projection, and recognizes the recovered shape by estimating the fast shape descriptor coefficients and the parameter perimeter/sup 2//area. In the method, the number of missing boundary points need not be known. The method is simple and fast. Experimental results from several 2-D shapes indicate that a satisfactory recognition rate can be obtained even when 20% of the boundary points are missing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Input impedance of double patch antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A moment method solution to the input impedance of a rectangular patch antenna with a parasitic element is presented. The grounded dielectric slab Green's function is derived. Entire basis expansion modes are used. It is found that the parasitic element improves the bandwidth of the antenna and provides an alternative method of impedance matching. The impedance behavior compares favorably with measured data presented by G. Dubost et al. (1986).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Convolutional coding system with tone calibrated technique for land mobile radio communication
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A data transmission system which combines convolutional coding with interleaving and modulation using the tone calibrated technique (TC) is presented for combating multipath fading usually encountered in land-mobile communication channels. By extracting and processing the faded pilot tone, coherent demodulation of the signal and soft-decision Viterbi decoding which channel amplitude measurement can be performed. The irreducible error rate is also reduced and good error performance is obtained. The performance in land mobile radio channels of the system is analyzed. Numerical results for the system with rate 1/2 optimum codes of constraint length k=3 to 7 are also provided.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The effect of shadowing on GMSK land mobile radio system
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Gaussian-filtered minimum-shift keying (GMSK) is proposed as effective digital modulation for mobile radio systems. The performance for GMSK is analyzed. Cochannel interference probabilities are evaluated for mobile radio systems operating in an environment where the fading is mitigated by adopting diversity reception. The protection ratio of the modulation and the cochannel interference probabilities are used to calculate the reuse distance and the number of channel sets needed for a cellular system. The conclusion is that the number of channel sets needed increases rapidly with the increase of standard deviation as the interference probability is fixed. With a high standard deviation users will suffer high interference and it is suggested that a greater reuse distance be used. For a given interference probability, a high protection ratio required by the modulation scheme will also increase reuse distance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modeling and performance evaluation of distributed systems as part of the development of ruggedized control and command systems
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Recently developed ruggedized command control information systems (CCIS) are distributed systems which usually include heterogeneous hardware and software. The authors introduce modelling techniques used for performance evaluation of CCIS. CCIS are composed of processing centers linked together through wide-area networks. These centers are distributed systems of computers connected through local area networks. Processing centers include databases as well as application software packages running concurrently on different computers. A model has been built using a queuing network formalism to forecast the different computers and link loads under various hypotheses. An appropriate dimensioning of the system and load balancing have been determined to help avoid bottlenecks at an early design stage. Moreover, the evaluation of response times on very complex applications and message processing has been used to validate the system's architecture.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The error control strategies for cut-through switching networks
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Error control strategies for cut-through switching networks are studied. Owing to the high speed and low bit-error-rate qualities of digital carrier systems or optical transmission systems, it seems unnecessary to link control functions at every node of the network. The error control done only at destination node (ECDN) strategy is therefore proposed. It is compared with the error control done at every node (ECEN) strategy from the viewpoints of transfer delay and buffer requirement. Through numerical examples, it is shown that the ECDN strategy performs better than the ECEN strategy if the increment of traffic intensity due to the error control functions at every node is not negligible. A simulation is also provided to support the validity of the analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Towards a speech oriented programming environment
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors present first results from a research project designed to improve the man-machine interaction and in particular to utilize speech recognition and natural language interfaces in the programming environment of the LCAP/3090 parallel supercomputer. An outline of the whole project is given and two specific applications being developed are described: scientific text dictation and a speech understanding system for Fortran debugging. The first application is based on the Tangora speech recognition system. Research in the debugging project is focused particularly on the natural language module.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The effects of Ricean fading channel on fast frequency hopping spread spectrum communication systems
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The performance of a fast frequency-hopped multilevel frequency-shift keying (FFH/MFSK) system operating through noisy, fading multipath channels is investigated. Additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and Rice distribution with random-to-specular ratio (K) are used to model the microcellular environment. The effect of a Ricean fading channel on user capacity is evaluated. Expressions are derived for the bit error rate of the OOK modulation scheme in the Ricean fading channel. At an average bit error rate of 10/sup -3/ and with perfect transmission (where the only degradation is due to mutual interference), the system capacity and the spectrum efficiency are found to be 209 users and 33.44% respectively. In microcellular environments the system capacity and spectrum efficiency are found to be 169 and 27.2% respectively, at the same error rate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of data and fax communications in Hong Kong
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The author outlines the historical development of data services in Hong Kong Telephone since 1978, and also outlines the current and future development potential for data transport and facsimile services. The focus is on new service developments driven by customer demand rather than technological innovation. The evolution of the packet switching service named Datapak is described. The regulatory arrangements reached in 1978 caused Hong Kong Telephone to introduce independent registration of fax lines, leading in 1981 to the transfer of all fax lines to electronic switching systems. This discrimination of facsimile service assured users of a high-quality transmission within the Hong Kong public switched telephone network. Growth trends for data and fax services are analyzed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Pattern design of TV transmitting antenna by optimization
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The field pattern of a reflector-type transmitting antenna to cover the service area of a TV station was obtained by optimization. Studies were made for reflectors with cross sections of a square and an octagon. The desired pattern was obtained by the application of the GTD approach. The design methods and the tolerance investigation are considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modifications of optical fiber voltage sensor
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The use of the electro-optic effect in crystalline quartz to form a passive optical fiber voltage sensor is described. The underlying principle and the temperature characteristics of the probe and modal noise of the fibers are discussed. Some modifications are mentioned. The selection of a broad spectral bandwidth source and a multimode fiber with large core can reduce the modal noise. A prism with a suitable kind of glass material is designed which can improve the temperature characteristic. The experimental results show that the measurement stability of the optical fiber voltage sensor is better than 1%.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of polarization fluctuation in a single-mode optical fiber
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The polarization fluctuation (PF) of a single-mode optical fiber output is discussed from the perspective of probability on the poincare sphere. The authors analyze the PF of the fiber from the point of view that the fiber has not only linear birefringence fluctuation but also circular birefringence fluctuation. The authors discuss PF theoretically by using the method of Imai and Matsumoto (1988). However, the results are more general since there are both linear and circular effects in an optical fiber.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Message encryption in a X.400 message handling system
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors describe a message security mechanism and its implementation on an experimental X.400 message handling system (MHS). An X.400 MHS usually consists of a number of heterogeneous machines communicating in an open system interconnection (OSI) environment which may be subjected to a security threat. A model is set up to identify various levels of security in an MHS network. The security measures are provided at the network level, that is, between the originating and the recipient message transfer agents (MTAs). A decentralized public-key based message encryption algorithm is used to eliminate the requirement of a key distribution center. A set of protocol procedures is defined to enable the change of encryption key at an MTA. A windowing concept is applied to encryption keys to reduce the potential conflict of key changes due to nonuniform message delay through the network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Range data from stereo images of edge points
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The author presents an algorithm and implementation for recovering range data from stereo images of edge points. The recovered data are used for object identification and localization. Parallel laser light planes are projected on a polyhedral object. The light planes appear as a set of broken straight segments in images. Discontinuities along these straight segments correspond to normal discontinuities on the underlying surfaces. Points of discontinuities in the image are extracted as edge points and they lie on edges of the underlying object. Matching edge points between stereo images give range data. The matching algorithm uses the epipolar constraint, a relational constraint, and an ordering constraint. The range data can be arranged in order according to the light planes to which they belong. Experimental results of the matching process and the accuracy of recovered data are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The transmission capacity of Chinese speech on 3COM Ethernet for integrated voice/data transmission
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors examine the transmission capacity of Chinese speech on 3COM Ethernet under combined voice and data loads according to the statistical characteristics of Chinese speech. A simulation technique is used. The relationship between the speech transmission capacity and offered data traffic is studied. The research results show that voice real-time communication can be realized on 3COM Ethernet. When the offered data load is heavy, the voice transmission quality cannot be guaranteed. If the collision delay algorithm is modified, the transmission capacity of Chinese speech will be increased.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A framework for deductive database systems
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors investigate various aspects of the development of deductive database systems, which integrate logic into traditional relational database systems. The authors review the database language Datalog, a version of a logic programming language for deductive database systems. The efficiency issues of query processing in the context of two popular query processing methods, the magic-set method and the structural-analysis method, are discussed. SARP (structural approach to rule processing), a framework of deductive database systems based on structural analysis, is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An experiment on 560 Mb/s transmission system limited by mode partition noise and the statistic measuring method of laser diode mode partition characteristics
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A simple and accurate theory proposed by Jiang et al. (see Optical and Quantum Electronics, vol.22, p.23, 1990) to calculate the mode partition noise in single-mode fiber systems is shown to be in good agreement with the transmission experiment presented. The 560 Mb/s transmission experiment using the multilongitudinal mode laser diode is described and the result indicates that the transmission distance is limited to 10 km by the mode partition noise when 1-dB power penalty takes place. A statistical method is proposed to determine the k-parameter of laser diodes modulated by quasi-random RZ binary signals. The k-parameter is the most important parameter to describe the mode partition characteristics of laser diodes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Numerical and experimental studies of the structural effect in symmetric PFA Y-junctions
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors present a numerical analysis of the structural effect of single-mode symmetric Y-junctions using a phase front accelerator (PFA) and other low-loss wide-angle designs. The beam propagation method (BPM) was used for the numerical simulation. The authors show how the structural effect can reduce the transmission loss significantly with various PFA parameters. The transmission loss is then compared with those in similar designs investigated by Weissman et al. (1989) and Rangaraj et al. (1989). The authors analyze and compare the reduction of transmission loss in Y-junctions using the structural effect, truncated normal and truncated structural design. For half-branching angles larger than 1 degrees , the proposed truncated structural design will offer lower transmission loss.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Image coding using weighted cosine transform
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A new orthogonal transform, called weighted cosine transform (WCT), is developed for digital image coding applications. The new transform is characterized. The transform matrix is the weighted version of that in the discrete cosine transform (DCT). Various commonly used criteria based on the one-dimensional and two-dimensional Markov models have shown that the performance of the order-8 and order-16 WCT is better than the DCT and the phase-shift cosine transform (PSCT), which is an improved version of the DCT. A fast computational algorithm for the WCT is also derived, which, however, requires more computational efforts than the DCT.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of an object-oriented front-end to a relational database system
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors describe the implementation of an object-oriented SQL (structured query language) front-end, called OOSQL, for the IBM DB2 relational database system. The restricted semantic entity-relationship model is used as the data model. The syntax of OOSQL is based on the syntax of SQL, which is the database language for DB2. SQL was chosen as the basis because it is expressive, powerful, and provides an easy evolution for DB2 SQL users. The authors modify and extend SQL by providing object management functions. OOSQL relies on the features of DB2 for dealing with concurrency, transaction management, integrity, and security. OOSQL provides constructors for object definition of any type, including recursive objects and complex objects. A prototype of the front-end described here has been successfully implemented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Engineering aspects of HDTV systems: the nonbroadcast applications of HDTV
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A broad range of nonbroadcast applications can be foreseen for HDTV. Some of them have already been implemented and have proved to be attractive and promising. A list of such applications is given and several of them are briefly analyzed.
