These applications consist of movie production; theaters; electronic publishing; TV commercials; catalog TV displays; telemedicine; medical still picture files; medical education; museums and zoos; educational applications related natural science and the arts, and HDTV lectures; computer-aided design; and observation and surveillance systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hierarchical image vector quantizer using gradient-Laplacian subspace distortion
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A new hierarchical mean-residual image vector quantization (HMRIVQ) technique using a general four-dimensional gradient-Laplacian subspace distortion (GLSD) is proposed. The GLSD is used for design and implementation of different block sizes of the HMRIVQ. Therefore, the computational and storage costs of the encoder are significantly reduced. The HMRIVQ can also achieve a very high compression rate for low detailed images. A performance comparison of the HMRIVQ using Euclidean distortion and the general four-dimensional GLSD is also given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the performance of the alternating maximum likelihood notching algorithm
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Simulation results are presented to demonstrate that the alternating maximum likelihood notching algorithm (AMNA) outperforms the iterative quadratic maximum likelihood (IQML) algorithm for low signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) cases. Moreover, it is shown that further improvement of the AMNA can be accomplished by using an elaborate two-dimensional slant search to adjust two bearing estimates simultaneously. This not only improves the accuracy but also results in faster convergence speed and higher resolution, especially for the cases of closely spaced sources. In addition, the algorithm is very suitable for hardware implementation through the concurrent Schur recursions and the associated pipelined combiner-lattice structure, thus making this improved algorithm more competitive in practical applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automatic train regulation system-a new concept in computerization of train control system
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The author describes the recently introduced automatic train regulation system (ATR), which forms an integral part of the nonvital train control subsystem. ATR is a distributed processing system with microcomputer-based workstations providing the user interface. The workstations connect to a schedule regulation subsystem, either by means of an Ethernet local area network (LAN) or remotely over serial links. A gateway is provided to interconnect the ATR LAN to the existing automatic train supervision computer system. ATR includes algorithms to ensure that train movements are controlled accurately, during both normal and distributed operation, by adjusting platform dwells, interstation run times and terminus turnaround times. Other features incorporated into ATR include emergency help screens, performance monitoring, short line working, and energy optimization.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel BOA type polarization independent optical switch
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors propose a new model of BOA type polarization independent 2*2 optical waveguide switch, based on z-cut LiNbO/sub 3/ substrate. It possesses a novel three-piece electrode system, which is easy to fabricate and has never been used before. The device still keeps the advantage of low loss on z-cut LiNbO/sub 3/, but has a higher switching voltage compared with that of the x-cut. Taking into consideration the fabrication conditions, they conclude that this type of BOA switch can be a polarization independent optical switch with low crosstalk, comparatively low switching voltage, and low insertion loss.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Planning CCS network penetration areas
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors describe the methodology used to designate the stored program control (SPC) switches as signaling end points (SEPs) in a common channel signaling (CCS) network. The proposed methodology contains a scheme for identifying the SEPs in each signaling region according to the region's potential and need for CCS network access. It estimates the number of equivalent SPC subscriber lines (ESSL) that will have access to the services requiring CCS capability for the network. It uses a heuristic approach to determine the SPC switch locations, both existing and planned, that match the number of total SEP subscriber lines and meet some preferential treatment criteria. Finally, using the methodology, a deployment plan is proposed for the SEPs in four planning phases of a case study.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of adaptive equalizer for digital subscriber loop using 2B1Q code
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: An adaptive equalizer structure for a digital subscriber loop using 2B1Q code is presented to combat intersymbol interference (ISI). A shaping filter is introduced to eliminate the precursor ISI. The design of this adaptive equalizer is based on a decision feedback equalizer (DFE) structure without feedforward section employing a clipped least-mean-square algorithm for estimating the postcursor of the channel's impulse response. A new variable stepsize method and a shape-oriented adjustment method are used to improve the convergence speed of the adaptive equalizer. Software simulation demonstrates the feasibility of the algorithm and structure. A hardware circuit is implemented using a logic cell array for real-time testing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distributed solutions to the mutual exclusion problem
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors propose the token path method for achieving mutual exclusion in distributed computing systems. The nodes in the distributed system interact only with their neighbors. There is no central control exercised. The node which wishes to execute the critical section perturbs the existing token path and waits for the token. When the token arrives at the node, the processes which request control for executing the section are given permission to execute the section according to some local policy. After that, the token is routed to another node which has requested the token. All messages are routed on the edges of the spanning tree of the system, which helps to reduce the number of messages. The nondeterministic selection of one-of-many critical sections is also presented, and a solution using the token path method is proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Facsimile signal processing for Chinese characters
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A facsimile (fax) signal processing system designed for filtering documents with printed Chinese characters is described. Filtering algorithms are applied to remove noise corrupting the image scanned by the fax machine and to preserve the edges. A total of six filtering algorithms have been chosen for investigation, namely, weighted average filter, separable median filter, median with checking filter, Lee's filter, gradient inverse filter and rotating variance filter. Documents containing Chinese characters are scanned and then stored in the RAM of a personal computer. Random noise is then added, and filtering performed. Experimental results show that all of the six algorithms are capable of removing some of the noise. However, the median filter demonstrated the best noise-removing and edge-preserving capabilities, speed of operation, and ease of implementation for both small- and large-size Chinese characters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An efficient register allocation for a WAM PROLOG compiler
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors outline an experiment on Warren abstract machine (WAM) based compiler technology. In preparation for a self-configured PROLOG system on a multi-node transputer network, a sequential PROLOG compiler is needed as a test bed. The compiler generates intermediate WAM codes, enhancing both the efficiency and portability. Another feature used by the compiler is an efficient register allocation mechanism. The WAM's parameter passing convention uses register k to pass the kth parameter to a procedure. Since the number of registers in the transputer is limited, data movements between registers are inevitable. The register allocation scheme minimizes data movement, and is somewhat different from that of minimizing the number of loads and stores in a conventional machine.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parallel Gaussian elimination for banded matrix-a computational model
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A parallel Gaussian elimination technique for the solution of a system of equations of the form Ax=C, where A is a banded matrix, is modeled as an acyclic directed graph. This graph is useful in the identification of parallel operations, the minimum absolute completion time for the solution process and the minimum number of processors required to solve it in minimum time. Hu's (1961) level scheduling strategy is used for scheduling operations to processors. The absolute minimum completion time sets a limit on the speedup; it is dependent on the order of the A matrix and is independent of the bandwidth. The minimum number of processors required to complete the solution process is fixed by the bandwidth and is independent of the order of the A matrix. A method of incorporating communication aspects in between processors in four kinds of interconnections is also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A modified contour generation thinning algorithm
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A modified contour generation thinning algorithm is proposed. It uses three pieces of information to process a contour pixel, compared with four in the case of the original algorithm and nine in the case of a typical sequential or parallel algorithm. This is possible because of the sequential nature of the algorithm, so that as far as a contour pixel is concerned, its predecessor does not take part in the computation of the new contour. Rather, the directions of the contour pixel with respect to the last generated pixel are used. This information together with the status of the contour pixel and its chain code will enable the new contour to be generated. This modification led to a reduction in coding effect, while maintaining the same speed as the original algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: DHT: diagonally hybridized tree is an efficient VLSI structure for parallel computation
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A new tree-based VLSI architecture called a diagonally hybridized tree (DHT) is proposed. DHT requires less hardware in terms of number of processors, connecting links and layout area compared to a mesh-of-tree of comparable size. By mapping a number of representative problems on DHT, the suitability of DHT for parallel computation is demonstrated. The results show that DHT with a sequential host can be used as a general-purpose parallel computer. A scheme is also given to tolerate faults in DHT by using spare processing elements (PEs) and links. It is shown that, asymptotically, DHT can tolerate O(N) faults by using O(N) spare PEs and O(N) spare links.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The prospects of telecommunication in Hong Kong
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Various aspects of the telecommunication services in Hong Kong are presented. The topics discussed are the domestic networks; the international network; types of telecommunication services; the cable TV network; international connections; new telecommunication-based industry; R&D in the telecommunication industry; and R&D support of the service integration network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ISDN trial in Taiwan, ROC
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The author describes the first integrated services digital network (ISDN) in Taiwan, deployed in 1989. The ISDN trial, with customized applications for different business customers, introduced ISDN from the end-user's perspective. ISDN offers Taiwan business and residential customers with any combination of voice, data and image services. With the use of the basic rate transmission extension, the ISDN trial can reach virtually every corner in Taiwan. Applications included in the ISDN trial are described. The trial involved the telephone company as the service provider and the network provider, other customer premises equipment (CPE) vendors, and end-customers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automatic control of gain and phase deviations in a dual-branch receiver
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A method of deriving the error signals for correcting the gain and phase deviations in a dual-branch receiver is described. This is based on separating the wanted signal and image signal components with an offset frequency between the transmitted carrier and the frequency of the first local oscillator. The correction process is adaptive and it operates continuously in the presence of modulation. A specific FM receiver architecture with remodulation has been chosen for illustration. However, the scheme described is also applicable for AM and single-sideband demodulation. The operation of the proposed scheme has been confirmed both by computer simulations and by experiments using a laboratory breadboard received.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Static intelligent backtracking restricted and-parallelism execution model
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A complete static intelligent backtracking restricted and-parallel (RAP) execution model with five new instructions and a modified backtracking algorithm is described. A RAP supporting static intelligent backtracking abstract machine simulator is discussed. The simulator generates run-time statistics such as total run-time steps and total number of failures, etc., and runs a program in a round-robin fashion as it simulates an instruction on each of the multiple processors. Simulation results show that the total number of execution steps is decreased. Some failures which send a remote message and interrupt their parents in the RAP execution model are more expensive than in the sequential model because of the cost of the interprocessor communication. The total number of failures is decreased, thereby minimizing interprocessor communication cost. The simulation results show that the performance of a RAP abstract machine is improved by static intelligent backtracking.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: FIR filter design by using the composite property mapping algorithm
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The notion of composite property mapping (CPM) introduced by Cadzow (see IEEE Trans. Acoust., Speech, Signal Processing, vol.36, p.49-62, 1988) is applied to finite impulse response (FIR) digital filter design. The result is a simple and transparent algorithm that could synthesize low-pass, high-pass, and bandpass filters with linear phase. Examples of FIR filter design are shown for low-pass, high-pass and bandpass specifications. Compared with other approaches the CPM algorithm is simple to program and converges quickly. An interesting feature of the present technique is that the computation time required is independent of the order of the filter since the computation complexity depends only on the dimension of the discrete Fourier transform selected.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: DSP-based implementation of Viterbi decoder for trellis-coded 8PSK
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The potential performance of four-state trellis-coded octal phase shift keying (8PSK) systems with different hardware complexities was evaluated by computer simulations. The experimental trellis coded 8PSK prototype described is designed to comply with the specification of a conventional SCPC/QPSK modem operating at a 64 kb/s data rate. To ensure full compatibility, the major filtering and IF-circuit sections of the existing SCPC/QPSK system remain unchanged. Only the QPSK modulator and demodulator are replaced with a four-state coded 8PSK encoder-modulator and demodulator-decoder. An implementation of a soft-decision Viterbi decoder for four-state trellis-coded 8PSK systems which is based on a single-chip digital signal processor is shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: NUMERIS ISDN in France: 1990 National Coverage
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The author considers France Telecom's strategy for the development of NUMERIS, the integrated services digital network (ISDN) in France. France Telecom's strategy for the development of NUMERIS is based on four main aspects: a fast national coverage, the definition of attractive tariffs, the development of international interconnections, and the development of applications. The author briefly considers the results of this policy. Based on this strategy France Telecom estimates the number of NUMERIS accesses in 1995 to be 500000.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A robust, low complexity 5.0 kbps stochastic coder for a noisy satellite channel
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A code excited linear predictive coding (CELP) based coder operating at 5065 bps is presented. The coder uses a self-excitation sequence for long-term prediction in addition to a fixed codebook populated with stochastic multipulse vectors as the excitation signal. The authors describe how the complexity of the coder is reduced, and present methods of increasing its spectral robustness, thus making it a suitable candidate for mobile satellite communication. The complexity is greatly reduced by using overlapping codevectors in both the adaptive and multipulse codebook. For robustness a filter correction scheme is derived, which, together with frame repetition techniques, will let the coder operate with little perceivable degradation in burst durations up to 40 ms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MAC-the European system for satellite broadcasting
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors explain the basic details of the MAC/packet family of systems adopted for all high power satellite broadcasting in Europe and the details of the D-MAC/packet member of the family and why it was chosen in the United Kingdom. In particular, the author describes some of the major technical and commercial benefits, with emphasis on the capability of the MAC-packet system to be used in the future for extended and high definition television (EDTV and HDTV) in a manner compatible with all the MAC packet receivers existing at the time of introduction of the new services.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: IIDAT-an intelligent interface design automation tool
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors present an integrated design automation system, IIDAT, for the design of microprocessor-based intelligent interfaces. It is implemented on the basis of a knowledge-based expert system to support the following functions: automatic design of microprocessor-based intelligent interface (MII) adapters from the specification at system level; automatic generation of control programs for handling MII; and, automatic linking to printed-circuit-board layout and circuit simulation packages. In addition, several functions are contained to realize a modularized, hierarchical, and flexible design automation tool.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An ISDN multimedia conference bridge
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: An architecture is presented for a network-based multimedia conference bridge. The bridge is attached to a central office switch or PBX as an adjunct processor. The basic functions of the bridge are conference management, voice bridging, packet data multicast, and circuit data multicast. By providing point-to-multipoint data services, the conference bridge addresses a lack in the standard services provided on the integrated services digital network (ISDN) and enables the terminal equipment to utilize the limited bandwidth of the ISDN basic rate interface more efficiently. The system was based on the networking requirements of the Rapport multimedia conferencing system and is primarily intended to support multiparty multimedia conferencing, but is also suitable as a general purpose platform for many other applications or enhanced services. In addition to a general architecture, a specific implementation is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A specification approach to artificial neural network design
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A specification-based simulation environment is proposed to address three issues in developing an artificial neural network (ANN) simulation environment. First, the concurrent aspect of an ANN system should be described. Second, design errors should be detected as early as possible. Third, the three distinct components of an ANN should be described separately and clearly. A dataflow specification approach is proposed to address these issues. It has two major characteristics: explicit specification for concurrency; and extensive checking for design errors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ISDN-PAS: an ISDN performance analysis system
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The integrated services digital network performance analysis system (ISDN-PAS) is a software tool developed for analyzing the performance of voice calls on ISDN. It takes raw call control data collected from the D-channel of the basic rate interface (BRI) of digital subscriber loops (DSL), reconstructs the original call control sequences, and generates performance statistics for the switches and networks. ISDN-PAS is written in C and runs in either a Unix or an MS-DOS environment. Owing to its general-purpose design, it can be used to analyze the performance of basically any ISDN configuration-whether emulated or a real end-user environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Flexible system techniques for future personable mobile communications
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The universal mobile telecommunication system (UMTS) currently being studied under the European RACE mobile project has defined a mission to achieve a pocket communicator for universal access to all telecommunication services by the year 2000. The key features will be the introduction of a mixed cell architecture with microcells overlaying macrocells, and a flexible air interface with adaptive bit rates. A versatile fixed network infrastructure with the capabilities of an intelligent network and compatibility with the future broadband and existing networks will also be implemented. The author focuses on the vital technologies which are crucial for the realization of the UMTS. The potential of the UMTS for Europe and worldwide are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of the maintainability of object-oriented software
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The experiment described supports the claim that systems developed with object-oriented languages are more maintainable than those developed with procedural languages. In this empirical study, student subjects determined the maintainability of systems developed with two languages by performing maintenance tasks on two functionally identical large programs, one written in an object-oriented language and the other written in a procedural language. Maintenance times, error counts, change counts, and programmers' impressions were collected. The analysis of the data from this experiment showed that systems using object-oriented languages are indeed more maintainable than those built with procedural languages.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New concepts of ATM network performance specifications
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors summarize the performance deterioration mechanism in complete and interworking asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) networks connected with existing networks and propose common performance specification concepts for multimedia services. Representative ATM performance parameters based on these concepts, in particular the observability of impairments at each portion boundary point, are proposed for network performance design. Finally, network performance objectives using the parameters are considered from the viewpoint of customer satisfaction and the physical performance of network facilities in actual environments.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The evolving intelligent network architecture
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors analyze an evolving service-independent intelligent network (IN) architectural platform. This IN architecture and its platform capabilities are evolvable from existing IN implementations. Existing INs offer the PTTs the benefits of early service revenues and operational experience. The evolving platform described here offers the flexibility for a larger variety of services, faster feature introduction, and greater customer control. Some possible synergies between IN and the integrated services digital network (ISDN) are also discussed. The authors describe some industry and standards activities on IN.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Protocol issues in interconnecting ISDN, IN, and LAN
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The author discusses some of the protocol design and implementation issues in interconnecting integrated services digital networks (ISDN), intelligent networks (IN), and local area networks (LAN). An internetworking architecture for a heterogeneous intelligent network that consists of network-resident intelligent peripherals and three subnetworks, a telephone network, a LAN, and an ISDN, is presented. Design issues and problems encountered in the implementation of four protocol conversion facilities for a heterogeneous intelligent network testbed are analyzed. The testbed allows multimedia real-time communications/messaging among LAN workstations with logically associated telephones and ISDN voice/data terminals with a stylus pen and transparent tablet on top of a bitmap screen.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new self-stabilizing bridge protocol for extended-LANs
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: Various solutions to the problem of combating bridge/link failures exist, most noticeably the spanning tree algorithm (STA) by R. Perlman (1985). Solutions based on a loop detect packet were proposed by R. Perlman and G. Varghese (1988) but never presented a viable alternative to work based on the STA. A more powerful loop detect packet based algorithm is described. The problems which plagued the previous loop detect approach are dealt with, and further extensions proposed. This algorithm is for multiple port local/remote bridges.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The ship model-a new computational model for distributed systems
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors present a new model of distributed computation called the ship model which helps solve the problem of location in a distributed system. In this model all entities are represented by ships. A ship contains both code and data and zero or more threads of control and represents a location into which other ships may move. Ships communicate by moving ships between each other. By representing location with ships, the ship mobility primitive unifies both code migration and inter-entity communication. Distributed programs can use mobility to capitalize on locality of reference and trade computation for communication. Not only can low speed lines be more effectively utilized, but network traffic in high-speed networks can be greatly reduced and interface to network services can be made simpler. A comparison with related work is also given along with a description of a prototype implementation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On designing a reconfigurable fault-tolerant pyramid tree network architecture
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: A new dynamically reconfigurable modular approach for pyramid tree network architecture is presented. A module, in which three primary processing elements (PEs) are supported by a spare processing element (SP), can be considered as a basic building block and it perfectly suits the VLSI design methodology in forming the complete fault-tolerant pyramid tree. Reconfiguration of the PEs is simple and local to the module. Since SPs can be shared across the module boundaries, multiple PE failures in a module can be tolerated. It is also shown that in addition to PE failures, this design can tolerate up to a certain extent SP failures as well. A switch structure, a simple reconfiguration algorithm, and a VLSI layout of the design are also presented. The reliability analysis shows a substantial increase in the system reliability of the proposed design over the nonredundant architecture. A yield analysis comes up with a promising result regarding single-chip implementation of the pyramid tree.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Knowledge engineering: the design of intelligent computers
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The author provides an overview of the current research and development directions in knowledge engineering, classifying research problems in the area according to three attributes: (a) completeness of knowledge in the environment, (b) accuracy of knowledge available in the environment, and (c) knowledge about the objective and/or specifications of the problem. Approaches to solving problems in this area are discussed, and challenges that lie ahead are examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A request/response protocol for ISO remote operations
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The authors describe the request/response protocol (RRP) which provides protocol support for ISO remote operations. RRP requires no separate protocol data unit (PDU) transfer to establish or release an association. Data transfer is efficient in terms of network utilization, unnecessary retransmissions and acknowledgements. RRP assumes an unsequenced, unreliable, and error prone datagram service. RRP segments and concatenates data too large to be transmitted by the underlying network. It uses selective retransmission to help deal with receiver overrun. RRP optionally monitors client reachability, and monitors server reachability while the client has an outstanding request. RRP is especially efficient for server applications requiring a large number of short-lived connections which transfer small amounts of data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the monitoring of remote procedure call programs
publicationTitle: IEEE TENCON'90: 1990 IEEE Region 10 Conference on Computer and Communication Systems. Conference Proceedings
abstract: The author presents the design and implementation of a remote procedure call (RPC)-oriented program monitor which records all events of an RPC-oriented program's execution in the monitor's database. Facilities are provided for programmers to define, choose, and combine events that will be recorded. The monitor has several managing servers which record the events of monitored program parts of their hosts into their local event databases. By using an ordering method, all events of an RPC program can be partially ordered and the event graphs of all program parts can be built. These event graphs are then used to replay the program's execution. Facilities are also provided to define combined events, to control the replay process, and to view the details of the message part of an event.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
